title: India-Born Jai Moondra Takes Record 6 for 26 as Ireland Level Namibia Series
excerpt: Moondra's six-wicket haul bowled Namibia out for 168 as Ireland won the fourth ODI by 130 runs to set up a Sunday decider at 2-2.
body:
• Ireland beat Namibia by 130 runs in the fourth ODI in Windhoek, scoring 298 for 8 and bowling the hosts out for 168 in 41 overs.
  • India-born seamer Jai Moondra took 6 for 26, the best ODI figures by an Ireland bowler, passing Josh Little's 6 for 36 against Zimbabwe in 2023.
  • Tim Tector made 73 and Curtis Campher 66, with Ireland scoring 101 runs in the final 10 overs.
  • The five-match series is level at 2-2, with the decider scheduled for Sunday, November 1.

Jai Moondra produced the best bowling figures by an Ireland player in one-day international cricket, taking 6 for 26 to bowl Namibia out for 168 and secure a 130-run win in the fourth ODI in Windhoek on Friday. The result levelled the five-match series at 2-2, according to Cricbuzz.

Ireland recover to post 298

Namibia, chasing a series-clinching win after taking the previous two matches, chose to bowl first. JJ Smit removed Andrew Balbirnie and Ruben Trumpelmann dismissed Cade Carmichael, leaving Ireland watchful at just above three runs an over after 15 overs. Tim Tector then accelerated, hitting successive sixes on his way to 73.

The innings changed late. Curtis Campher made 66, George Dockrell added late runs, and Jordan Neill hit two sixes as Ireland scored 101 runs from the final 10 overs to finish on 298 for 8, Cricket World reported. Campher reached his fifty from 39 balls in an innings that included six sixes in total across the sources' accounts.

Moondra wrecks the chase

Namibia had passed 300 in the previous two games, but Moondra struck three times in his opening spell to reduce the hosts to 32 for 3, removing Malan Kruger, Jan Frylinck and Louren Steenkamp. Gerhard Erasmus was trapped leg-before by Liam McCarthy, and at 45 for 5 the contest was effectively over.

Zane Green made 45 and added 57 with Ruben Trumpelmann for the eighth wicket, the only sustained resistance. Moondra returned after the drinks break, bowled Green, completed his five-wicket haul by bowling Trumpelmann, and took his sixth wicket with the final ball of his spell to close the innings. His 6 for 26 from 10 overs, including a maiden, eclipsed Josh Little's 6 for 36 against Zimbabwe in 2023 as Ireland's ODI record.

A series turned on its head

Namibia had seized momentum by winning the second and third matches, passing 300 in both, and a third straight win on Friday would have closed out the series with a game to spare. Instead, Ireland's bowlers produced their most disciplined display of the tour. The hosts managed only 29 runs in the opening powerplay for the loss of two wickets, and by the 16th over they had collapsed to 50 for 5, with Moondra at the centre of the damage.

Ireland's total also owed much to its finish. After reaching 150 in the 31st over, the visitors added 127 runs from the last 83 balls, as Campher and George Dockrell, who finished unbeaten on 47 from 34 balls, shifted the pressure onto Namibia's bowlers. Smit was Namibia's most successful bowler, but the target of 299 proved well beyond a batting line-up that never recovered from Moondra's opening spell.

Decider on Sunday

Moondra, the India-born 29-year-old seamer, was named Player of the Match. Ireland's win sets up a winner-takes-all fifth ODI on Sunday, November 1, with the series tied after Namibia had led following back-to-back wins in the middle matches.
